name: Rending
overview: Scripture presents rending, particularly of garments, as a profound outward expression of grief, distress, or repentance, as seen when Jacob and Reuben rent their clothes upon hearing troubling news about Joseph (Genesis 37:29, 34). This act also signifies deep emotional turmoil or mourning, exemplified by Ezra's response to Israel's sin (Ezra 9:3) and the lament of Jephthah (Judges 11:35). Beyond personal affliction, rending serves a figurative role symbolizing the breakdown or dissolution of a kingdom, illustrating the gravity and finality of such events as reflected in the various instances of rending among God's people (Genesis 44:13; Numbers 14:6).
